messages:
leah.support: Escalation from customer (ticket #CS-4921). They're missing audit events in Splunk for certain event types (user_activity, key_rotation) starting 2026-03-15 03:00 UTC. They forwarded our S3 export via the SIEM forwarder and report schema mismatches and missing KMS metadata (kms_key_id). Sample event_id: evt_9f2b3c. Can we triage? :eyes:

 tom.sec-eng: On it. Do we have their forwarder config and a sample raw object from S3? Also which export bucket/prefix?

 leah.support: Bucket: redwood-audit-exports-prod, prefix: exports/2026/03/15/. Provided sample object (pasted below). They also included forwarder logs showing KMS AccessDenied errors.

 leah.support: ```
{ "event_id":"evt_9f2b3c", "type":"key_rotation", "timestamp":"2026-03-15T03:12:07Z", "user":"svc-account@acme", "kms_key_id":null, "kms_cipher":"aes_gcm" }
```

 vik.sre: If kms_key_id is null that suggests KMS metadata got stripped during export or we failed to decrypt the envelope. Could be our export lambda didn't include metadata for some encrypted objects. Any kms-related errors in forwarder logs?

 leah.support: Forwarder log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z ERROR forwarder.s3_to_splunk Failed to decrypt object s3://redwood-audit-exports-prod/exports/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz KMS:AccessDenied
2026-03-15T03:12:09Z WARN forwarder.schema Mapper couldn't find field kms_key_id, dropping field
```

 marcos.eng-platform: This looks like a permissions/CMK policy issue. Check if the CMK was rotated at 2026-03-14T22:00Z — rotation can remove the forwarder role from the key grants. Also verify the bucket lifecycle: customer expects 365d retention but our bucket shows 90d.

 tom.sec-eng: Action items:
1) Confirm CMK rotation history and grants.
2) Run a query on export manifests for events with null kms_key_id.
3) Check forwarder pod env for role assumption vs stale AWS keys.
4) Coordinate a backfill to Splunk for the missing day.

 vik.sre: Quick repro command to inspect the file locally:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-audit-exports-prod/exports/2026/03/15/part-0001.gz - | zcat | jq -r '.event_id + " " + (.kms_key_id // "null")'
```
I ran that and saw ~1200 events with null kms_key_id in that file.

 leah.support: Customer is asking for a backfill and also wants a Splunk field mapping doc (they have strict index mappings). Is there a canonical mapping we provide?

 marcos.eng-platform: Yes, share docs/audit/splunk-mapping.md (mapping changed 2025-09). Expected event wrapper snippet:
```
# Splunk HEC event structure
{ "event": { "id": "event_id", "ts": "timestamp", "type": "type", "user": "user", "metadata": {"kms_key_id": "kms_key_id", "region": "region"} } }
```

 tom.sec-eng: For immediate mitigation we can re-run the forwarder with an IAM role that has kms:Decrypt on the CMK and reprocess those objects. Vik, can you restart with role=forwarder-backfill-role and tail logs? :thumbsup:

 vik.sre: Starting restart now.

 audit-forwarder-bot: restart triggered by vik.sre using role forwarder-backfill-role

 audit-forwarder-bot: Forwarder restart acknowledged. Backfill worker started for prefix exports/2026/03/15/. ETA ~45m.

 leah.support: I'll update the customer with ETA and ask for any additional SIEM mapping constraints.

 tom.sec-eng: Also add a retention check — customer expected 365 days but bucket lifecycle shows 90 days. Raise to platform for policy change and notify compliance.

 leah.support: Noted. Created infra ticket INFRA-7628 and added compliance.

 marcos.eng-platform: Postmortem checklist: ensure exporter preserves kms metadata, confirm CMK grant automation includes forwarder roles, and create an alert for >0% events with null kms_key_id in daily export pipeline.

 leah.support: Thanks team. I'll collect logs and sync after backfill completes. :white_check_mark:
